prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active forms that made possible incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B033 as a single prize part for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. Round 1 showed that all six of us reached it by arguing the science, and nobody found a flaw in the chain from hormone physiology (Holst on the secretion and actions of the active forms in humans, Drucker on proglucagon-derived peptide and receptor biology, Mojsov on identification and synthesis of the active truncated peptide) to the drugs. The discovery is original, the mechanism is understood, independent randomized outcome trials in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal disease have confirmed benefit, and the impact is at its peak. On the chair's first question, I judge the achievement to be the physiology. A Physiology or Medicine prize can acknowledge the drugs in its citation wording, and the citation I propose does so by saying the discoveries made the therapies possible. It should not make drug development a credited achievement, because that would shift the prize toward industrial optimisation of a mechanism that others had already defined.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weak point. I cannot settle Mojsov against Habener from the supplied record, and I do not want to pretend that my recollection of the priority history is a verified finding. My basis for keeping her is narrow: the contribution I credit is the identification and synthesis of the biologically active truncated peptide, a distinct step that the physiology and the later pharmacology both depended on. If the committee finds that this step cannot be separated from Habener's group, the correct response is to reopen the slot openly, not to fill it quietly. The omission of Knudsen is a real cost that the three-person cap forces, and a critic can fairly say the prize honours the hormone and not the medicines. I accept that cost as a deliberate choice and would want it recorded as one.

responses.point: He keeps Knudsen as a possible third slot only if Mojsov's priority cannot be defended, and he lists CAR-T and optogenetics as alternatives.
responses.response: I agree with his condition, and it is where I land too. Knudsen replaces Mojsov only if the committee concludes the active-peptide step cannot be credited to her, and then the citation would have to change to describe incretin physiology together with long-acting agonist development, which is a different and less clean achievement. I disagree that optogenetics should stand above the other alternatives. Six credited names against a cap of three means the prize would cut people whose priority claims cannot be separated from those who stay, and I read that as a defect in the configuration, not a detail to settle later.

responses.point: He says my omission of BCR-ABL from his opening eight needs defending, and he argues that it is an application of oncogene and kinase work credited to others, so he places it below CAR-T and GLP-1.
responses.response: His objection has changed my ordering. In round 1 I put B032 second. The prize-defining idea, that a constitutively active oncogenic kinase is a druggable target, rests on BCR-ABL and Philadelphia chromosome work outside Lydon, Druker and Sawyers, so the trio mainly rewards drug discovery and clinical proof. Durable survival in CML is as mature as any result on the list, but maturity does not repair a credit gap at the level of the idea. I now put B026 ahead of B032 and keep B032 as the second alternative only because its clinical evidence is the strongest of the secondary candidates.

responses.point: She would not place BCR-ABL ahead of CAR-T or TNF blockade, and she asks for any TNF allocation to be checked against earlier cytokine work.
responses.response: I agree on the ordering against CAR-T. On TNF blockade, I still read B051 as a clean pair with unquestionable maturity, but her point about earlier TNF biology and antibody engineering by people outside Feldmann and Maini is the same kind of gap that lowers B032 for me, so I treat the two consistently. I would not put B051 in my two alternatives. If she wants it taken up as a second part, the cost would be cutting the GLP-1 trio by one or more names, and I do not think a TNF part justifies that cost this year.

responses.point: As chair he proposes June and Sadelain for CAR-T, treating Rosenberg's adoptive cell therapy as a separate line and Eshhar's chimeric receptor concept as outside the credited names, and he asks whether a two-part prize is acceptable.
responses.response: I would not support a two-part prize this year. With the three-person cap, adding a second part would cut the GLP-1 part to one or two names, which would break the attribution logic that makes B033 defensible, and members have not identified a second achievement with a clean credit set. On B026, I hold that June and Sadelain can be credited honestly only if the citation names the design and clinical proof of genetically engineered T cells, and not the chimeric receptor concept itself. The Eshhar gap is therefore a reason to keep it as a first alternative and not as a preferred part, and it explains why I would cut Rosenberg from any CAR-T trio.

responses.point: He argues that adding Knudsen would turn the prize into a drug-development award, and that nusinersen (B045) is strong but may be slightly early.
responses.response: I agree that crediting Knudsen would change the kind of prize this is, and I would not add her in place of Drucker or Holst under any scenario. I am more willing than he is to say that this is a real loss. Her work is what turned the hormone into a durable therapy, and the citation should therefore refer to therapies made possible by the physiology. On B045, I still read the evidence as strong but still short on the generality of the splice-switching platform, so I keep it off my alternatives list this year and would consider it later.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's contribution to the identification and synthesis of the active peptide can be credited in distinction to Habener and colleagues. I cannot verify the priority record from the supplied materials and I rely on memory for part of it.
Whether the committee, in discussing the physiology of GLP-1 against drug development, will accept leaving out Knudsen as a recorded choice, or will hold that this reading makes the prize incomplete.
Whether June and Sadelain can be credited by a citation that is honest about Eshhar and Rosenberg. If not, B026 is unfit for 2026 and the alternative would need to be reconsidered.
statement.conflict_note: No shortlisted candidate involves my own work. My profile records the co-authored 2016 spatial transcriptomics paper and eight co-authored works with Rickard Sandberg, and co-authors including Ernfors, Frisen and Castelo-Branco, but none is a credited name on B033, B026 or B032, so I find no specific conflict and no recusal is needed. Shared Karolinska Institutet affiliation is not treated as a conflict.
